sections.h2: Which office bills and assesses property in Rockingham County?
sections.html:
The Tax Administration office handles both sides of the bill. In Rockingham County the jobs of assessor and collector are combined under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division. You can reach it at the Rockingham County Governmental Center, 371 NC Hwy 65, Reidsville, on weekdays. Call 336-342-8305 or write to PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375, which is the same address used for payments.

The assessment division lists, appraises and assesses real property, business personal property and individual personal property, and it also handles ownership transfers and record maintenance. The collection division bills and collects current and delinquent taxes for the county, the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts. A house inside a town can therefore carry several levies.

Sellers in Rockingham County should know the scale of the roll. The county describes itself as having about 55,800 real estate parcels, 4,000 businesses, 98,800 registered motor vehicles and 4,350 personal property manufactured homes. Rates are set by the Board of County Commissioners, each fire district and each city or town council, and the county says they are established in June with bills mailed in late July.

sections.h2: What is the Rockingham County tax calendar?
sections.html:
Bills fall due on September 1 each year. The county's own page said the 2025 bills could be paid with no interest through January 5, 2026, which matches the state rule that interest starts on January 6.

After January 5 the state adds a flat two percent, and from February 1 on it adds three-fourths of a percent for every month or part of a month. A prepayment discount can exist if the county or a town adopted one, so ask the collector about the current bill. A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

Rockingham County lists these ways to pay:

  • A card payment online through the county's payment-service link, or an e-check through a second link
  • A call to 1-866-251-3264, with the bill in hand
  • A check mailed to Rockingham County Tax Collector, PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375-0068
  • Counter service at the Governmental Center, which you should confirm with the office

The county sets rates in June and mails bills in late July, so a seller listing in spring is dealing with last year's rate until the new budget passes.

sections.h2: What are the review levels for a Rockingham County value?
sections.html:
Four levels exist, and the county page names all of them. You begin with an appraiser and finish, if needed, at the state Court of Appeals.

The informal level means calling the Real Property Division so an appraiser can recheck the record. The county says this is open from January 1 until the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. That Board is chosen by the county commissioners, answers to no tax office staff, and starts hearing cases in April.

The four levels of review on the Rockingham County appeal page
LevelWho decidesDetail on the county page
1Real Property DivisionAppraiser review, January 1 through Board adjournment
2Board of Equalization and ReviewAppointed by the commissioners, hearings from April
3NC Property Tax CommissionFive members in Raleigh, hearings by application and appointment
4NC Court of AppealsLast resort for a dissatisfied owner

Under the statutes, the written request precedes the Board's adjournment, and a further appeal to the Commission follows within 30 days of the mailed decision. The county adds that changes in value between reappraisals are limited by G.S. 105-287.

sections.h2: Why did Rockingham County reappraise in 2024?
sections.html:
State sales ratio studies pushed it into an early reappraisal. The county's FAQ explains that a ratio below 85% or above 115% forces a reappraisal within three years, and Rockingham's ratio came in at 91.25% for 2020 sales, 77.86% for 2021 sales and 69.55% for 2022 sales. That meant tax values were far under market prices after the strong market that began in 2020.

Tax Administration worked with Piner Appraisal on the 2024 reappraisal. The appraisers compared property cards with what they saw on site, tracked sales since the last reappraisal and studied rents and building costs. To value land, they grouped the county into about 500 zones called neighborhoods and set a land rate for each from local sales.

  • New values took effect for 2024 tax bills and stay fixed until the next reappraisal, apart from changes the statutes allow.
  • Notices of change of value went out by mail or email in early April 2024.
  • The Board of Equalization and Review convened April 3, 2024 and adjourned May 8, 2024, and appeals were due before that date. Those dates have passed.
  • A property card can be obtained at the Tax Administration office in Wentworth or viewed on the county website.

The county's own test for a fair value is simple: if the assessed figure is close to a price you would think reasonable when listing the house, the appraisal is correct. Ask the office when the next reappraisal is scheduled.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can Rockingham County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
Three state programs exist and each owner may use just one. The county's Tax Forms page carries the 2026 Application for Property Tax Relief, the disability certification for the homestead exclusion and the certification for the disabled veteran exclusion. The same page lists a Present Use Value deferment application, a builder's exclusion and a Tax Certification Request form.

In short, the homestead exclusion protects the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value for older or disabled owners who stay under the $38,800 income limit that the 2026 state form prints. The disabled veteran exclusion takes off the first $45,000 regardless of age or income. The circuit breaker caps the bill at a share of income and defers the rest as a lien.

A deferral stays on the property. It comes due for the preceding three years if the owner sells, dies or stops living in the house, so a seller on that program should get a payoff early. The county's FAQ points owners with questions on exemptions to the Tax Office at 336-342-8250.

sections.h2: What does a Rockingham County seller owe in property tax at closing?
sections.html:
Expect to cover your share of the current year's bill plus any earlier balance. The lien for a year's tax attaches to the parcel as of the January listing date, and interest and costs ride along with it, so an overdue amount has to be cleared before a buyer gets clean title.

If a bill stays unpaid, the county can sue much as a lender would, and a courthouse auction may follow. Redeeming before the court confirms means paying the tax plus penalties, interest and costs.

Before listing, ask the collection division for a payoff on every parcel number, fire district charges included. Your closing attorney then prorates the current year. If you plan a fast sale of a house with back taxes, expect the title company to pay the balance from your proceeds at settlement.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Rockingham County property taxes?
faqs.a: You pay the Rockingham County Tax Collector, online, by phone at 1-866-251-3264, or by mail to PO Box 68 in Wentworth. Keep your bill handy, since the phone option requires it.

faqs.q: Is the Tax Assessor a different office from the Tax Collector in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: No. Rockingham County combines the assessor and collector roles under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division inside the same office.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my value by phone?
faqs.a: Yes for the informal step. You can call the Real Property Division and speak with an appraiser, who will review the record and value. The formal step before the Board of Equalization and Review must be requested in writing on the county form.

faqs.q: What if I sell my Rockingham County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: The lien follows the parcel, so the balance must be paid for title to pass cleanly. Your closing attorney normally pays it from your sale proceeds, so request a payoff amount from the collection division before closing.

faqs.q: Which towns send a tax bill collected by the county?
faqs.a: Besides the county bill, the collection division collects for the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts, so one parcel can carry several levies.
